cells.tense: You already hold the small structure others stand in — and you can judge a thing squarely while it is still being felt.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Pick one arrangement you built when it was right and that now only runs on habit. Set it down — stop carrying it, say it's finished — and then see what your hands are holding.
cells.core:
You can feel a thing all the way through and still judge it squarely. That's the skill — you rule from inside the feeling instead of over the top of it, and the small structures you build hold because of it. Whoever stands in one is steadier for the fact. You do it quietly, and it's yours.

Keep an arrangement only as long as it's true. The next one you build, ask whether it still serves the people inside, and if it doesn't, set it down — not repaired, just finished. You know the kind: the ones the people inside are already working around. Ending it costs some comfort. It's also the only thing that frees the space it took for something living.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel all of it and still call a thing fair.
cells.verb: Weighing feeling fairly enough that people can live with the ruling
cells.place: The room where the pattern that others move inside gets drawn

cells.tense: Where the structure is yours to hold, you'll be settling a hurt before it has had its hour.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: The next thing that lands wrong, carry it through a day with no ruling attached — a stone with no wall chosen yet. Let it finish being felt before you decide what it means.
cells.core:
Where the structure is yours to hold, you're readying the ruling before the feeling has finished. A hurt arrives and by evening you've settled whether it was fair, who tipped it, what should happen — decided neatly, decided early, landing on people who didn't know a verdict was coming. You feel it too. That's the part nobody sees.

Holding is not judging. The next upset close by, carry it for a day with no answer attached: what is it, who is in it, what's actually being weighed. A load of stone, nothing built yet. The right call is almost no worse for a night's keeping, and whoever it concerns will still be there when you're ready to make it.
cells.sheetLine: You're ruling on feelings before they finish being felt.
cells.verb: Weighing feeling fairly enough that people can live with the ruling
cells.place: The room where the pattern that others move inside gets drawn

cells.tense: Where the pattern got drawn, something unfairness had been standing in — and it went quiet before anyone could weigh it.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Take one unfair situation you're still carrying and put it on paper in sequence — this, then that, then the next. Keep feeling words off the page, then read it back and let the page hold it.
cells.core:
Something between the people where you live stopped being balanced a while back, and it stayed that way. The arrangement rusted, someone carries more than their share, the thing that is known and unnamed sits in the middle of the room. It used to sort itself out when you were in the thick of it. Here, you've left the bench and there's no one else in that chair.

The method comes back before the nerve does. There's one unfair situation you keep turning over — one arrangement that rusted and nobody named. Put what happened on paper in sequence, no feeling words, and read it back. The imbalance gets visible on paper before it gets visible in a room, and the call arrives half made.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what's unfair and you've stopped calling it.
cells.verb: Weighing feeling fairly enough that people can live with the ruling
cells.place: The room where the pattern that others move inside gets drawn

cells.tense: In this corner of things, you're holding the shape for others while it doesn't register as yours at all.
cells.act: listen as a student of it
cells.ask: At the next dispute close by, hear the whole thing as someone new to it, before you do what you'd normally do to settle it. Say nothing. Just hear it.
cells.core:
Things between the people close to you hold together — not by accident, and not as a rumour. You make a call and one side softens; you shift a word or a weight and a room settles. To your own telling, you're not in the middle of anything. But the ones who have been steadied by it go on behaving as though they know who did it.

Try hearing your way into it instead of running it. At the next dispute close by, take it in from the start as though the whole thing were new, and only afterward do what you normally do to level it. Half of what you do happens before the words come together. Listening that slowly, the working gets counted from inside, by its maker.
cells.sheetLine: The balance between people is kept, by you, while you say you stay out of it.
cells.verb: Weighing feeling fairly enough that people can live with the ruling
cells.place: The room where the pattern that others move inside gets drawn
